text:
maria: Heads up — multiple customers (AcmeHealth, WellPath) reporting 504/gateway timeouts hitting hosted inference in us-west-2. Started ~10:20 PDT, persistent for ~15m. Customer escalation open.
aj: Confirming. Proxy/gateway logs show upstream 504 + 'no ready endpoints'. KEDA metrics look weird: ScaledObject didn't spawn extra replicas despite queue spike.
kevin: Quick paste of relevant lines from node/pod events and scaler logs:
```
10:19:22 kubelet: Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 504
10:19:23 keda-operator: ScaledObject 'tenant-acmehealth' metricsource mismatch: expected 'queue_len' got 'queue-length' -> ignoring metric
10:19:24 hpa-controller: currentReplicas=1 desiredReplicas=1 (no scale event)
10:20:05 proxy: upstream timeout after 30s, returning 504 to client
```
sam: Support note — AcmeHealth says they also saw a few 403s earlier (auth token rotation) but main impact is 504s and timeouts when queue is hot. They want repro steps and mitigation.
sre-bot: Alert: autoscaler-threshold crossed for tenant-acmehealth at 10:18:59, but cooldown annotation prevented new scale until 10:23:59. ScaledObject.cooldown=300s.
maria: Repro steps we've validated locally: 1) send burst 120–200 RPS to the tenant route 2) watch queue metric spike (queue_len > 500) 3) gateway returns 504 once queue latency > 20s. Note: single replica currently serving large model -> long warmup.
kevin: Root cause hypothesis: combination of 1) KEDA scaledobject config mismatch (metric name), 2) long container warmup for model (cold init ~45s), 3) high cooldown on scaledobject preventing quick additional replicas. Also readiness probe timeout low so pods marked unready until warmup complete.
aj: Immediate mitigation options: lower scaledobject.cooldown to 30s, bump minReplicas for tenant pool to 3, increase readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds and timeoutSeconds (e.g., timeoutSeconds=60), and add quick fallback routing to a smaller model variant.
oncall: Applying quick fixes: setting tenant-acmehealth.minReplicas=3 now, patching scaledobject.cooldown=30s for this tenant. Monitoring after patch.
support-ic: Customer notified with temporary workaround: add client-side exponential backoff (retry window 60s) and optional fallback endpoint to cached responses. They accepted and will test.
maria: I've started a collector runbook: include exact k8s events, KEDA logs, and gateway traces. Please upload pod logs + scaledobject yaml.
kevin: Pasting scaledobject snippet that caused mismatch:
```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: tenant-acmehealth
spec:
  cooldownPeriod: 300 # too long for spikes
  triggers:
    - type: prometheus
      metadata:
        serverAddress: http://prometheus:9090
        metricName: queue-length # should be 'queue_len' per our scaler config
```
kevin: Also attaching k8s events excerpt (copied):
"Normal" ScalingScheduled 10:18:59 scaledobject-controller Scheduled scaling check
"Warning" ScalingSkipped 10:18:59 scaledobject-controller Metric mismatch: metricName 'queue-length' not found
"Normal" PodStarted 10:19:40 kubelet Started container, warming model (45s)
"Warning" ReadinessFailed 10:19:55 kubelet Readiness probe failed (timeout)
"Normal" ProxyTimeout 10:20:05 proxy Upstream timeout -> 504 to client

aj: Next steps (who):
- kevin: collect full pod logs + scaledobject/controller logs and drop in incident folder (ASAP)
- maria: draft customer-facing timeline & workaround notes (done)
- oncall: keep minReplicas bumped and monitor for 30m, then revert if stable
- eng-runtime: propose a runbook change to require scaledobject cooldown <= 60s for tenant pools with bursty traffic and add unit test for metricName validation on deploy

sam: Flagging this for a follow-up retro: we should consider prewarm jobs for large-model tenants (image pull + model preload) and a routing policy to route to smaller models during scale events.
maria: Thanks — I'll file a postmortem and link the runbook + timeline. For now, oncall, please confirm whether error rate fell after the fixes.
oncall: Confirming: error rate dropped ~70% in next 10m, queue length returned to normal. Will keep monitoring until 11:00 PDT.
support-ic: Customer acknowledged workaround and will keep retries active. Marking escalation as 'monitoring' for now.
maria: Great. Follow-up action items assigned in notes. Closing thread when postmortem + logs uploaded.
